item.title: Miyazaki Mango — Guide
item.description: Miyazaki’s warm, sunny climate makes it Japan’s leading producer of premium mangoes, and its top-grade fruit is a byword for luxury. The most famous are the ‘Taiyō no Tamago’ (‘Eggs of the Sun’) — flawless, jewel-like mangoes that must meet strict standards for size, sugar content and a deep, even red colour to earn the brand name. Left to ripen fully on the tree until they naturally drop into protective nets, they are picked at peak perfection, giving an intensely sweet, richly fragrant, silky-smooth flesh with almost no fibre.

item.title: Tottori Sand-Dune Melons & Farm Tours — Guide
item.description: The same free-draining sandy soil that forms the Tottori Sand Dunes is turned to advantage in the farms behind them, where the loose, sun-warmed sand and long sunshine hours produce unusually sweet fruit. Tottori’s sand-grown melons are its most prized crop, alongside sand-cultivated Rakkyo shallots, watermelons and grapes. Farm tours in the melon season let visitors see how crops are grown in the challenging sandy ground, learn about the region’s distinctive ‘sand agriculture’, and taste ripe Tottori melon — sweet, fragrant and best eaten within days of picking — at its early-summer peak.

item.title: Yubari Melon — Guide
item.description: The Yubari melon (Yubari King) is Hokkaido’s most famous fruit and one of Japan’s ultimate luxury foods, grown in the former coal-mining town of Yubari in central Hokkaido. A premium cantaloupe-type melon with beautifully netted skin and vivid orange flesh, it’s prized for its intense sweetness, juicy tenderness and rich aroma, the result of careful cultivation in Yubari’s ideal soil and climate. Yubari melons are graded by strict standards, and the finest specimens are legendary for fetching astonishing prices at the season’s first auctions — the top pairs have sold for millions of yen, making headlines each year.
